subject: Post-call: fit evidence, schema checks, and tool-call kickoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@healthbridge.ai>, Tom O'Neil <tom.oneil@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: fit evidence, schema checks, and tool-call kickoff

Hi Sophie and Tom — great to meet you both today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of the call
- Goal: replace heuristic document extraction service with a structured-output pipeline that emits patient-summary JSONs and triggers downstream billing tools via function calls.
- Key constraints: 200ms token latency SLO for single-record extracts; PII must never leave customer-hosted VPC for private mode; schema must pass strict JSON Schema conformance for all required fields.
- Main risk: hallucination of diagnosis codes and inconsistent field types in earlier benchmarks.

Recommended immediate actions (owners & timing)
1) Benchmarks & model recommendation (Ben + Aditya) — share model-fit evidence and top 2 model variants by E2E F1 and hallucination rate. Deliverable: spreadsheet + quick dashboard link by EOD tomorrow.
2) Schema & test harness (Karthik) — draft JSON Schema, golden prompt set, and automated conformance runner (local and CI) for your engineers to run. Target: draft by Tue 4/17.
3) Tool/function-call playbook (Monica) — define retry/backoff semantics and idempotency guarantees for the billing webhook. First pass by next week.

Attachments included: acme-model-benchmarks-20280412.xlsx (high-level), acme-promptset-v1.jsonl (seed prompts), schema-tests-runbook.md (initial plan).

Next meeting
- Suggest a 45 min technical kickoff (Redwood SRE + your infra + Acme dev lead) to run through the schema and data flow. Proposed slots: Mon 4/16 10–10:45am PT or Tue 4/17 2–2:45pm PT.

Open questions for Acme
- What proportion of documents will need deep context (>4k tokens)?
- Do you have an internal mapping of diagnosis code sources we should prefer (claims vs EHR vs lab exports)?

Thanks — I’ll push the benchmark spreadsheet and a short deck in the next email.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Ben — thanks, that recap looks good. A couple quick clarifications before you guys slice the benchmarks: 

1) Latency: our interactive UI requires 150–200ms median for single-record extracts; tail can be higher but start with median target.
2) Data residency: for PHI-containing fields we will want Private deployment in our Azure VNet — can you confirm the schema-runner can be run in a customer-managed environment?

Also, Tom and I would like the benchmark to include an explicit hallucination metric for structured fields (false_positive_fields / total_required_fields). If you can add that column to the spreadsheet it will make tradeoffs clearer.

We can do Mon 4/16 10am PT for the kickoff — marking that slot tentatively.

— Sophie
Director of Product, HealthBridge AI
Sophie.Lane@healthbridge.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: fit evidence, schema checks, and tool-call kickoff — benchmarks attached

Hi all — attached is a compact benchmark export and a short note on methodology. High-level recommendations:

- Top model candidate: "redwood-mix-13b-int8" (best precision on entity fields, 1.8% median hallucination on required fields, median token latency ~140ms with our continuous-batching config).
- Backup option for strict cost vs latency: "redwood-lite-7b-q4" (higher hallucination tradeoff, but 3–4x cheaper on per-token CPU/GPU time; good when you run heavy batching in Dedicated).

Benchmarks included
- E2E F1 (structured fields), hallucination_rate, median_latency, 95p_latency, token_cost_estimate.
- Each metric measured on your 1k-sample seed set (attached in promptset).

What we changed from your baseline
- Prompt scaffolding to lock types and enumerations (see examples in promptset).
- Post-processing step: we suggest a lightweight verifier that rejects fields with low confidence and returns a tool-call to human QC for those records (Monica will draft the workflow).

Attachments: acme-model-benchmarks-20280412.xlsx, acme-promptset-v1.jsonl

Ben — please flag any redlines on methodology. Aditya and I are available for a short walkthrough Monday morning prior to the kickoff if useful.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@healthbridge.ai>, Tom O'Neil <tom.oneil@acmehealth.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 13:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: JSON Schema + test harness plan (for kickoff)

Hi team — attaching a short plan in-body for visibility; I’ll push a markdown doc to the Drive tonight.

Draft schema approach
- Root object: patient_summary (required)
  - patient_id: string, pattern: UUID
  - encounter_date: string, format: date-time
  - diagnoses: array of objects (code:string, source:string enum["claims","ehr","lab"], confidence:number 0-1)
  - medications: array of objects (name:string, dosage:string, start_date:date)
  - billing_code: string (nullable)

Conformance & gating rules
- All required fields must be present and type-matched; any record failing schema that contains PHI must be routed to private human QC only.
- A light-weight verifier will run rules: numeric ranges, enumerations, code patterns. Failure mode: return structured error object + tool-call to /human_review endpoint.

Test harness (CI + local run)
- Seed prompts (acme-promptset-v1.jsonl) run through the runner; compare against golden labels.
- Metrics: field-level precision/recall, hallucination_rate (false_positive_fields / total_required_fields), schema_violation_rate.
- Integrations: the harness will emit SARIF-like artifacts to your repo for line-level fail/fix traceability.

Retries and idempotency for tool-calls
- Retry policy: exponential backoff up to 3 attempts for 5xx from billing endpoint; 4xx = fail + human alert.
- Idempotency: include request_id + idempotency_key (hash(patient_id, encounter_date, model_version)) so repeated deliveries are safe.

Open asks from Acme before kickoff:
1) A sample of 50 blueprints that contain edge-case diagnosis lists (we’ll use these to tune post-processing).
2) Confirm the billing webhook’s idempotency expectations (headers, accepted dedupe window).

I’ll upload schema-tests-runbook.md with examples and a minimal runner by EOD.

— Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
